answers.acts: What it acts on: its roll of properties and its connections, each billed by its meter each quarter; a household's request to be supplied, and notice that it has gone; and the notices it is given of land changing hands and of building work.

keeps.why: Its customer roll: the valuer's roll of each property it supplies is given to it, as valuations are given to a rating authority.
Its customer roll: each notice that land it supplies has changed hands is given to it.
Its network: the mains, services and connections it operates, with what its instruments read of them, are its own works and records (foundations-2 C3).

schema.description: whom the water bill goes to: the property's owner (by the roll) or the occupant (the connection's user), as the place's law has it
what the works' store holds when full (litres): what the daily draw keeps it at
the work that draws a kilolitre
the work that treats a kilolitre of wastewater and puts it back on the land
the water works (the world must say): where it draws from the river

works.source: the water works (the world must say): where it draws from the river

routines.what: Each day the works draws from the river what keeps its store full, and says so when the river cannot give it; and treats what the sewer brought back.
Before each round of bills a reader goes round the meters; then each bill is sent for the service charge and what its meter shows was used. How often the bills go out is the order's.
